title: How the ratchet keeps old messages safe

scenes.narration: Someone steals your phone's encryption key today. Can they read yesterday's messages? With a ratchet, no.
Every message gets its own key. A one-way function turns the current chain key into a message key and the next chain key. Then the old chain key is deleted.
It only turns forward, like a ratchet. A thief holding today's key cannot run the function backwards.
But they could still follow you forward. So with each reply, both phones swap fresh public keys and mix in a new shared secret. The chain restarts, and the thief is locked out again.
